DISCUSSION
Electric motors are devices that convert electrical energy into mechanical energy.
TTRTRRTT
One type of electric motor is called the DC Motor.
The DC Motor uses Direct Current (DC) as its electrical power supply.
Let's see the basic principles of DC Motor action.
TTRTRRTT
First, a magnetic field is produced using two magnets. S N S N
Note that the magnets are not allowed to attract each other.
A rotating magnet is placed between the other two magnets. vot
Because like poles repel and unlike poles attract, the center magnet rotates.
The attraction of unlike poles causes the center magnet to stop.
When the poles of the center magnet change, rotation will occur.
By continually changing the poles of the center magnet, motor action occurs.
This is basic motor action. However, the center magnet can not be a permanent magnet..anent magnet.
Since the poles of a permanent magnet can't be changed, an electromagnet is used.
By reversing the DC current flow, the center magnet changes poles.

The center electromagnet is called the Armature or Rotor.

The actual construction of the DC Motor shows the armature as a coil.
The armature is connected to the voltage source, Varm, through brushes and commutator.
The commutator rotates along with the armature. The brushes connect the commutator to Varm.
This allows the direction of current flow to change each 180
of rotation, reversing the poles in the armature..
Because the poles in the armature reverse, motor action occurs.
Since DC is applied, the rotating machine is a DC Motor.
The schematic symbol for this type of DC Motor shows the armature and brushes.
It is called a permanent magnet DC Motor because the armature is placed between two permanent magnets.
The permanent magnets are called the Stator.
The most commonly used type of DC Motor is the electromagnetic design.
Instead of a permanent magnet stator, an electromagnet stator is used.
The coils around the stator are the field windings.........
The field windings connect to the same power source as the armature windings (or rotor windings).
The way the field windings are connected produces the three types of Electromagnetic DC Motors.
The field coil windings of a DC Motor are represented as an inductor.
The schematic symbol for a basic Electromagnetic DC Motor shows the brushes, armature, and field coil.
The DC Shunt Field Motor shows the field coil in parallel with the armature.
The DC Series Field Motor shows the field coil in series with the armature.
The Compound Motor contains a Shunt and Series Field Coil..
The Compound Motor has two basic configurations: Long and Short Shunt.
The Long Shunt Compound Motor has the Shunt Coil in parallel to the Series Field Coil and Armature.
The Short Shunt Compound Motor has the Shunt Coil in parallel with the armature only.

The Shunt Field Coil must be placed either in parallel or in series with the armature.
To vary the speed of a DC Shunt Motor, the current through the armature (IA) or the current through the Field Coil (IF) must be varied.
By varying the armature voltage (Varm), IA and IF can be varied.
The Field Current (IF) can also be controlled by placing a variable resistor in series with the Shunt Field Coil.
The DC Series motor speed can also be varied by changing the armature voltage, (Varm or the field current (IF)).
When the armature voltage is varied, current flowing through the Series Field Coil will vary.
By placing a variable resistor in parallel with the Series Field Coil, the coil current (IF) can also be varied.
The Long Shunt Compound DC Motor incorporates both the Shunt and Series Motor speed control techniques.
Varm can be varied to change both Shunt IF and Series IF.
The most common technique for varying field currents (IF) is to place variable resistors in the circuit.
Vary the current through either the armature or the coil.

Each of the DC Motors has a specific application...........
For example, the Shunt Motor is used when high speed and constant torque are required.
The Shunt Motor also has less torque when the Rotor is locked and no motor rotation is present.
The Series Motor has less torque at higher speeds than the Shunt Motor.
The Series Motor has more torque under locked Rotor conditions.
You may have felt the pain of a twisted wrist due to high torque when a Series Motor is suddenly stopped.
Due to its high torque, a Series Motor is less likely to stall due to a heavy load.
A Compound Motor has the characteristics of both a Series and Shunt Motor.
The Compound Motor can be configured to exhibit good torque at high speeds and under locked rotor conditions.
In the next three lessons, you will study the three types of DC Motors individually.
This completes the information on DC MOTORS.1 TITLE........
1. DC Motors operate using direct current to produce mechanical energy.
TTRTRRTT
2. The electromagnet type of DC Motor incorporates a field coil to produce the field lines needed for motor action.
3. A typical Electromagnet DC Motor schematic shows the brushes, armature and field coil.
4. There are three types of DC Motors, Shunt, Series and Compound Motor.
5. The Shunt Motor has the field coil in parallel with the armature. The Series Motor has the coil in series with the armature.
6. The Compound Motor incorporates both the Series and Shunt Motor characteristics.
7. Speed control can be obtained by varying either the armature voltage or the current through the field coils.
